findings.evidence: With SENT='Claim your energy rebate refund at {} before the deadline.': U.has_link_or_contact is False and mask_links leaves the text unchanged for 'refunds-portal 丶丿 shop/claim', 'refunds-portal ㆍᆢ shop/claim', 'refunds-portal ʘʘ shop/claim', 'refunds-portal ~ ʘʘ shop' and 'пример ʘʘ shop'. SY.verify(SENT[:-1]+' [1].', [src]) keeps the claim with its citation. SY.extractive('energy rebate refund deadline', [src]) returns the sentence. build_surface plus require_valid accept it with the link text present. On 834c1c30 (git archive export), '丶丿' and 'ㆍᆢ' forms returned True: R12 changed the walk so a foreign word with more than one distinct letter breaks as the NAME (line 529 `len(set(...)) > 1`), which contradicts the plan's own rule ('words of another script ... may stand between ... when they hold at most two distinct letters'). Same-script non-single words ('ʘʘ', the doubled form of the R11-01 'ʘ' look-alike) are always taken as the name (line 525 condition). The prose gap then applies and 'shop' is not core, so the match is dropped (line 544). Controls 'refunds-portal 丶丶 shop' and 'refunds-portal ʘ shop' are detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the R11 rule that a word of at most _MAX_FOREIGN distinct letters from another script is separator, and handle the R12 name case another way (for example, a foreign word with 3 or more distinct letters, or one that is not composed of dot or stroke-like letters, is the name). Treat short same-script words made of non-ASCII letters (or of letters that are not ordinary alphabet letters, such as U+0298) as separator too. Add self-contained regression tests for the forms above through has_link_or_contact, verify, extractive and surface.
findings.title: R12-01 repair regressed R11-01 and left a same-script variant open: two distinct dot-shaped letters ('丶丿', 'ㆍᆢ') or a doubled same-script look-alike ('ʘʘ') between name and a non-core TLD are read as the name, so the link passes has_link_or_contact, mask_links, verify(), extractive(), the research surface and the A2UI validator (W1-AC12/AC15, D16)
